questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a content of the axilla?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly lists the cords of the brachial plexus as one of the contents of the axilla.

questions.question: The neurovascular structures in the axilla are vulnerable to injury when the arm is in which position?
questions.explanation: The text states that the structures are vulnerable to injury when the arm is abducted.

questions.question: The axillary artery is the main artery of which part of the body?
questions.explanation: The first sentence under the AXILLARY ARTERY heading states it is the main artery of the upper limb.

questions.question: At which border does the axillary artery begin?
options: Inner border of the second rib
Outer border of the first rib
Lower border of the teres major
Upper border of the pectoralis minor
questions.explanation: The text states it begins at the outer border of the first rib.

questions.question: The axillary artery is a continuation of which artery?
questions.explanation: It begins as the continuation of the subclavian artery.

questions.question: At which structure does the axillary artery end by becoming the brachial artery?
options: Outer border of the first rib
questions.explanation: The text states it ends by becoming the brachial artery at the lower border of the teres major.

questions.question: During its course through the axilla, the axillary artery runs nearer to which wall?
questions.explanation: It runs along the lateral wall nearer to the anterior wall than the posterior wall.

questions.question: Which muscle crosses the axillary artery on its superficial aspect?
questions.explanation: It is crossed on its superficial aspect by the pectoralis minor muscle.

questions.question: The pectoralis minor muscle divides the axillary artery into how many parts?
questions.explanation: The text states that the pectoralis minor divides the artery into three parts.

questions.question: Where is the axillary vein located in relation to the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states, "The axillary vein is medial to the artery throughout its course."

questions.question: The cords of the brachial plexus are arranged around which part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The text notes the cords are arranged around the second part of the artery.

questions.question: Which cord of the brachial plexus is located medially to the second part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table lists the medial cord of the brachial plexus as a medial relation of the second part.

questions.question: Which cord of the brachial plexus is located laterally to the second part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table lists the lateral cord of the brachial plexus as a lateral relation of the second part.

questions.question: Which nerve is listed as a posterior relation of the first part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table lists the long thoracic nerve as a posterior relation of the first part.

questions.question: Which structure is an anterior relation of the second part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table explicitly lists the pectoralis minor as the anterior relation of the second part.

questions.question: Which nerve is a posterior relation of the third part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table lists the radial nerve as a posterior relation of the third part.

questions.question: Which nerve is a lateral relation of the third part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The table lists the musculocutaneous nerve as the lateral relation of the third part.

questions.question: How many branches does the axillary artery give from its first part?
questions.explanation: The text states the axillary artery gives one branch from the first part.

questions.question: Which artery arises from the first part of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The text states the superior thoracic artery arises from the first part.

questions.question: The superior thoracic artery passes between which two muscles?
questions.explanation: The text notes it passes between the pectoralis major and minor muscles.

questions.question: At which border of the pectoralis minor does the thoraco-acromial artery emerge?
questions.explanation: The thoraco-acromial artery emerges at the upper border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: The thoraco-acromial artery pierces which fascia?
questions.explanation: The text states it pierces the clavipectoral fascia.

questions.question: Which of the following is a branch of the thoraco-acromial artery?
questions.explanation: The four branches are pectoral, deltoid, acromial, and clavicular.

questions.question: The lateral thoracic artery runs along which border of the pectoralis minor?
questions.explanation: The lateral thoracic artery emerges at and runs along the inferior border of the pectoralis minor.

questions.question: Which artery is the largest branch of the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly identifies the subscapular artery as the largest branch of the axillary artery.

questions.question: The circumflex scapular artery is a large branch of which artery?
questions.explanation: The text states the subscapular artery gives a large branch called the circumflex scapular artery.

questions.question: The posterior circumflex humeral artery passes backwards through which space?
questions.explanation: It passes through the quadrangular intermuscular space along with the axillary nerve.

questions.question: The anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries anastomose to form an arterial circle around which structure?
questions.explanation: They form an arterial circle around the surgical neck of the humerus.

questions.question: Which artery is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk that participates in the scapular anastomosis around the body of the scapula?
questions.explanation: The text lists the suprascapular artery as a branch of the thyrocervical trunk involved in this anastomosis.

questions.question: Clinically, what does the scapular anastomosis serve as if the subclavian or axillary arteries are blocked?
questions.explanation: It serves as a potential pathway (collateral circulation) to ensure adequate circulation to the upper limb.
